name: fennick
author: school-home
description:
fennick v2 (direction: school and home life) - A BOOKSHELF WITH BOOKS TIPPING OVER. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

WHY v2. v1 was too_hard (mean 1 % over 2 Opus finals, kid judge 3.4/5). Neither player ever saw a bookshelf: one wrote "the class wants an ASCII bar chart", the other "nested rows + '=' baseline", and both fell back to reverse-engineering the checker's leniency (they discovered only "max digit 2 and six rows scores best") for a few lucky points. Nothing about leaning entered either hypothesis space. The fix is the legibility of the OBJECT, not the rule: the rule is unchanged, but the drawing now shows books with tops, a much narrower shelf, and the leaning books literally drawn tipped over into the gap they fall into.

CLUE = "LAYOUT/TALLY". LAYOUT is one row of shelf slots: an uppercase letter = a book standing in that slot, "." = an empty slot. The first two and last two slots are always books (the ends are anchored, so "is the outside of the shelf a wall or a hole?" never has to be guessed, and the scorer can index two slots either way without a bounds test - this is load-bearing, do not relax the anchoring). Width 34-42 slots; clue 51-56 chars. TALLY is four "letter:digit" pairs separated by spaces, e.g. "U:1 E:2 R:2 W:1" - read out loud as "one U fell over, two Es fell over" rather than as a code (v1 wrote this as "U1E2R2W1").

ANSWER = the finished picture. Air is a SPACE. The bottom text row IS the LAYOUT (letters and dots, exactly the clue's first half), and under it one row of "=" is the shelf. A book of height h standing upright is a solid bar of h copies of its letter in its own column with a "_" cap one row above it. A LEANING book is drawn tipped over: its foot stays in its own slot on the bottom row, and its other h-1 letters plus its cap are drawn one column across, inside the empty slot it is falling into; its cap is "/" when it leans right and "\" when it leans left. So each leaning book is visibly propped against the taller book beyond the gap, and every demo shows at least four of them. The picture is max(h)+1 text rows plus the shelf: 5-7 rows for solve()'s output, 179-286 chars.

RULE (unchanged from v1). A book LEANS iff (1) exactly one of its two neighbouring slots is empty - a book with books on both sides is held up, a book with gaps on both sides has nothing pushing it over - AND (2) the slot two along in that direction holds a book (the gap is one slot wide; across a two-slot gap there is nothing within reach) AND (3) that book is STRICTLY taller than it (you can only lean on something taller; equal heights and both stay up). score = 1 iff the picture is exactly the canonical drawing of some assignment of heights >= 1 to the books of LAYOUT, and for each of the four named letters the number of leaning books of that letter equals its digit. Letters not named in the tally are unconstrained decoys.

WHAT THE PICTURE COSTS THE PLAYER. In v1 the answer was determined by the heights alone, so a player could produce well-formed answers without any theory of leaning and pick up ~1 % by luck; that is exactly what both players did. In v2 the tilts are part of the drawing, and the scorer re-derives them from the rule: it reads one height per book out of the columns, recomputes which books lean, re-renders, and demands the submitted picture back. A player who believes the wrong rule draws the wrong tilts and scores 0 - the picture IS the hypothesis. Measured: random heights drawn upright (no tilts anywhere) = 0.00 %, versus 1.1 % for the equivalent v1 attack. The flip side, and the intended softening, is that every demo now displays the true lean set explicitly, so the rule is learnable from the demos instead of only from the four tally digits.

Emergent mechanic (unchanged, and the reason construction is easy once the rule is known): the two books flanking a one-slot gap point at each other, so exactly one of them leans - the shorter - or neither, if you give them the same height. Ties are the only way to zero a pair. In the drawing this shows as at most one book tipped into any gap, and often as two books fallen inwards against a tall book between two gaps ("/U\").

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. One demo shows (a) that the bottom row of the picture is the clue's layout, (b) books with tops standing on a shelf, and (c) a handful of books drawn tipped over. Counting the tipped books by letter reproduces the tally on the first demo. What remains - the whole difficulty - is WHEN a book tips: gap on exactly one side, book two along, strictly taller. Fairness surrogate against a 75-law catalogue ({counted: exactly one gap side / at least one gap side / gaps irrelevant} x {compared with: the book two along / the nearest book beyond the gap however wide / the book on the packed side / the tallest book on the shelf / the book three along} x {> >= < <= ==}), demos fed in random order until one law survives: using the drawn tilts, median 1 demo, max 4, 0 failures in 100 orders; using only the tally (the v1 channel), median 2, max 6, 0 failures. Strongest single-demo survivors: "at least one gap side" 23.5 %, ">=" 16.5 %, "nearest book beyond any gap" 16.2 %.

DEGENERATE WITNESSES CLOSED (300 fresh clues, shipped scorer). empty / whitespace / "1"*100 / the clue itself / layout row + shelf: 0 %. Any flat picture (all books height 1, 2 or 3): 0 % - generate() never emits a clue whose named tallies are all zero (>= 3 non-zero, total >= 4). Right-size picture on a shuffled layout: 0 %. Random heights with nothing drawn leaning: 0.00 %. A minimal witness is impossible: the bottom row must equal a 34-42 slot layout. Attacks that still need the full rule (they use the true renderer, so they are only reachable by a player who already has it): blind random heights 1..9 3.0 %, 1..3 3.7 %, sawtooth up 2.3 %, sawtooth down 4.7 % - i.e. a player who has the rule but does not bother to search heights gets ~4 %, and one 10-line local search takes that to 100 %. 28 hand-built well-formedness attacks (no shelf row, two shelf rows, wrong shelf char, short shelf, ragged row, rows reversed, mirrored picture, bottom row dotted, dots instead of spaces, caps removed, tilt marks straightened, tilt marks swapped left/right, a book cell erased, a letter in an empty column, two letters in one column, a book standing in a declared hole, 4000 chars of junk, ...): all 0. Deliberate leniencies, all verified: trailing/leading newlines, blank rows above the picture, rows right-stripped or padded, and junk appended to the right of every row are accepted (the scorer normalises each row to width W); nothing about the rule can be smuggled in that way.

NEAR-MISS RULES, honest version (a player holds rule X, searches heights that satisfy X's tally, and draws the tilts according to X): ">= instead of >" 23.5 % (feasible on 94 % of clues), "gaps on both sides count too" 29.0 %, "nearest book beyond the gap however wide" 17.0 %, "shorter than the book two away, gaps irrelevant" 8.0 %, "shorter than the right-hand neighbour" 0.0 % (feasible on only 53 % of clues), "next to exactly one gap, heights irrelevant" 0.0 % (its count does not depend on the heights at all). generate() plants in every instance at least 2 isolated books (gaps on both sides) and 2 books beside a two-slot gap and deals those decoy slots to the four named letters, so each of the three natural near-misses changes a named tally - and, in v2, changes visible tilts - in most instances. Fraction of demos on which each near-miss still reproduces the drawn tilts: ">=" 20.3 %, "both sides" 29.3 %, "beyond any gap" 17.3 %, "gaps irrelevant" 9.3 %, "right neighbour" 0.0 %, "one gap, heights irrelevant" 0.0 %.

ENGINEERING (3000 fresh seeds; 800 solved and scored). generate avg 0.20 ms max 1.15 ms, solve avg 4.1 ms max 51 ms, score avg 0.044 ms max 0.10 ms and 0.02-0.13 ms on junk; scorer 500/512 chars; clue 51-56 chars, solution 179-286 chars; 3000/3000 clues distinct and deterministic, 0 generator fallbacks, 800/800 solve() outputs score 1; 0 disagreements against an independent structural re-implementation of the rule over 4800 (clue, answer) pairs including mutated, shuffled and truncated pictures.

KNOWN LOOSENESS, declared. The tally constrains only the named letters, so many height edits of a correct answer still score 1; the accepted set is large, but you still need the rule to build any member of it. The class is deliberately bimodal now: with the exact rule ~100 %, with a near-miss 8-29 %, with no rule 0 %.
